free_tier.stated: Free: EUR 0, free forever. Session 24h, Max players 10, Ports 1, Speed 10 Mbps, Latency Standard.

egress.terms: No byte allowance is published, on the pricing table or in the FAQ. The free plan states Session 24h, Max players 10, Ports 1, Speed 10 Mbps.; ingress: tcp+udp

interface_detail: A Windows tray app: sign in, pick a preset or a port, copy the address. No API or CLI is described.
tooling: PortPlay Windows app only; no CLI and no Linux client is offered
chaining: Needs a Windows host, so it composes with a Windows instance rather than a Linux one.

limits.value: Speed 10 Mbps on Free, 50 Mbps on Pro, 100+ Mbps on Pro Max
Session 24h on Free, 6 months on Pro, Unlimited on Pro Max

binding_note: The speed cap is the only number the vendor publishes, so it is named as the binding constraint.

identity_cost.detail: An account, or Google sign-in: 'Create an account or continue with Google. Getting started is fast and free.'

reliability_note: One port and 10 players on Free. The app reconnects automatically when the link drops. No statement on end-of-session behaviour or on idle reclamation.
confidence_note: One free session would show whether the assigned UDP port survives a reconnect and whether 10 Mbps is enforced per tunnel, per account or per session.

evidence.proved: Free is EUR 0 with Session 24h, Max players 10, Ports 1, Speed 10 Mbps; Pro is EUR 1.49 with 3 ports and 50 Mbps; Pro Max is EUR 4.99 with 10 ports
Arbitrary ports: 'Set the ports you need. Simple Voice Chat, Geyser, and other plugins that require an extra TCP or UDP port work too.'
FAQ: 'Java usually uses TCP port 25565, Bedrock and Geyser use UDP port 19132, and Simple Voice Chat uses UDP port 24454 by default.'
The sample address is play.portplay.net:25565, so a customer gets a shared hostname plus an assigned port, not an IP of their own

notes: The free allowance is a speed and a session length, not a byte quota. Because the endpoint is a vendor hostname plus a port, PortPlay demultiplexes UDP by port on a shared edge instead of spending an IP per customer, which is the structural reason it can give UDP away. Windows 10/11 only. Nothing on the site says what happens at the end of the 24h session.

extras.wg_detail: No WireGuard mode of its own, but the free port forwards any UDP a user names, so a WireGuard datagram addressed to the assigned host and port would pass. That is a reading of 'Any TCP/UDP port', not a test.
extras.volume_stated: No byte allowance is published, on the pricing table or in the FAQ. The free plan states Session 24h, Max players 10, Ports 1, Speed 10 Mbps.
extras.transit_note: The PortPlay relay carries the datagrams; the origin only makes an outbound connection.
